title: How much cheaper must a store's electricity be than a heat pump's for a sand heat store to deliver heat for less?
summary: Costs the sand store of energy-thermal with every capital cost, lifetime, O&M and efficiency read from PyPSA technology-data (Danish Energy Agency; Viswanathan et al. 2022, PNNL-33283) at pinned revisions, sizing it with the transient model run to cyclic steady state and comparing levelised cost of heat against an air-source heat pump. Store charged at EUR 0.05/kWh, house (10 MWh a year): cycled daily it is cheaper than a heat pump even when the pump's electricity costs 0.6 times as much, because the pump's own capital is most of its cost; weekly the pump's electricity must cost 3.3 times the store's to break even, monthly 13, seasonally 119 (222 m3 and EUR 1.53 of capital per kWh). At district size (5 GWh a year) 1.3, 1.9, 4.4 and 37 times, and a central hot-water tank beats sand at every cycle length. Corrected 2026-11-18: each cycle had been billed as a first charge from 10 C, which put the daily house ratio at 2.1. Not from a source: electricity prices (swept), 2,000 full-load hours, 0.5 m insulation, cycle counts. Limitations: the sand-store cost is a utility-scale figure, no heat exchanger is costed (favours the store), flat prices, constant COP, instant discharge.
lede: how much cheaper must electricity be for a sand heat store to beat a heat pump? Sourced costs (PyPSA technology-data) on the `energy-thermal` model, run to cyclic steady state: a house store cycled daily wins even at equal prices (ratio 0.6), weekly it needs the pump's electricity 3.3 times dearer, monthly 13, seasonal 119; corrected 2026-11-18 from 2.1 / 5.0 / 16 / 120, which billed every cycle from cold. Standby loss, not the sand, rules out seasonal storage.
